title: Smart Thermostat Rebate in Red Deer 2026: $50 From the City
desc: Red Deer's 2026 smart thermostat rebate pays $50 per City utility account for a qualifying ENERGY STAR smart thermostat bought this year. Who qualifies, the wiring check and how to apply.
h1: Smart Thermostat Rebate in Red Deer
lead: Red Deer is one of the few Alberta cities with its own home energy rebate. The City pays $50 when you swap your old thermostat for a qualifying smart one. It is small, but it is real money with a simple form. Here is who qualifies, what to buy, and the one wiring check to do before you shop.
cards_heading: What Red Deer homes can get
cards_intro: We re-read the City of Red Deer's rebate and energy efficiency pages on October 3, 2026. Both are linked at the bottom.

cards.title: City of Red Deer Smart Thermostat Rebate
cards.note: For a new smart thermostat from the qualifying list, bought in 2026 and installed in Red Deer. One rebate per City utility account. Applications close when the funds run out.

cards.title: Free thermal camera and toolkit loans
cards.note: The City says you can borrow a thermal imaging camera and an Energy & Water Conservation Toolkit from the Red Deer Public Library.

cards.title: Clean Energy Improvement Program
cards.note: Red Deer is not on Alberta Municipalities' list of residential CEIP locations, so there is no tax-bill financing here.

after_cards:
Check your wiring first

The City warns that most smart thermostats need a C wire (common wire) to give them steady power. Before you buy, take the cover off your old thermostat and look for a wire on the terminal marked C. If there isn't one, ask the store or an electrician which models will work, or whether an adapter is an option.
sections:
The City lists these rules. You must:

  • live in Red Deer and have a City of Red Deer utility account;
  • buy a new smart thermostat from the qualifying list in 2026 and install it at a Red Deer property;
  • not have used this program before;
  • not be using another funding program for it, such as the federal Greener Homes Grant and Loan (which has now ended anyway);
  • send a copy of your receipt showing the store, product, price and date.

It is one rebate per utility account, so a household gets one $50 payment even if it installs two thermostats.
What counts as a qualifying thermostat

The City's qualifying list links to the ENERGY STAR finder for certified connected thermostats sold in Canada. If a model is on that list, it should qualify. Check before you buy, and keep the receipt.

The City says space heating and cooling make up almost two-thirds of home energy use, and that a smart thermostat can lower energy use by 8% to 12%. Your own savings depend on your home and how you set your schedule.
Red Deer homes, by the numbers

The 2021 Census counted 40,515 households in Red Deer. About 53% live in single-detached houses and 65% own their home. About 34% of households live in homes built before 1981, and another 28% in homes built from 1981 to 2000.

Renters can apply only if they hold a City utility account, and should ask the landlord before changing a thermostat. Red Deer's average January low over the last ten years was about -14.3°C, and the coldest reading was -42.4°C. A smart thermostat won't make an old house warmer, but a schedule that lowers the heat while you sleep or are at work is an easy saving.
Make the most of it: borrow before you buy

A thermostat is a small step. To see where your home actually loses heat, borrow the free thermal camera from the Red Deer Public Library. It shows cold spots around windows, doors and attic hatches. The library's Energy & Water Conservation Toolkit helps you find which appliances and devices use the most power.

Since Red Deer has no CEIP financing and Alberta has no provincial rebates in 2026, these free tools are the cheapest way to plan bigger upgrades.
claim_heading: How to claim Red Deer's $50 rebate
claim_steps: Check your wiring for a C wire and pick a model on the ENERGY STAR certified connected thermostat list.
Buy it in 2026 and keep a receipt that shows the store, product, price and date.
Install it at your Red Deer home.
Fill in the Smart Thermostat Application Form from the City's rebate page and attach the receipt.
Apply soon: the City closes the program once this year's funds are spent.
faq: How much is the Red Deer smart thermostat rebate?
$50, one per City of Red Deer utility account.
Is the Red Deer thermostat rebate still open in 2026?
Yes, as of October 3, 2026. The City says it is an annual program and applications close when funds are spent, so apply soon after you buy.
New smart thermostats on the qualifying list the City links to: the ENERGY STAR list of certified connected thermostats for Canada.
Can I get the rebate for a thermostat I bought last year?
No. The thermostat must be bought in 2026.
Does Red Deer have CEIP financing?
No. Red Deer is not on Alberta Municipalities' list of residential CEIP locations.
